lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Photo Editing: Changing Pictures
lesson.summary: Crop, resize, recolour and clone pictures, spot edited photos and make an honest poster.
learning_objectives: Explain how digital pictures are made of pixels and how crop, resize, recolour and clone change them
Spot clues that a picture may be edited
Edit honestly, keep originals and credit the maker

standards.text: Select, use and combine a variety of software on digital devices to design and create digital content
Use technology safely, respectfully and responsibly; recognise acceptable and unacceptable behaviour

success_criteria: I can explain pixels, crop, recolour and clone
I can spot clues of editing
I can make an honest poster that credits the maker
lesson.real_life: Editing Eid or Hunza holiday photos for a family album or school poster, and checking which photos online have been changed.

warm_up.prompt: What does a computer use to store a picture?
warm_up.explanation: A digital picture is stored as numbers.

warm_up.prompt: What does it mean to edit something?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we edit pictures, and how do we stay honest?
blocks.say: Today we find out how pictures are made and changed. Can we always trust what a photo shows?

blocks.alt: A dirt road leading toward snow-capped mountains under a deep blue sky, with a tree on the right
blocks.caption: A mountain road. Every part of a digital photo is made of tiny squares.
blocks.credit: Photo by Vinu T on Unsplash
blocks.say: Zara found this mountain photo. Zoom in far enough and the picture turns into tiny squares.

blocks.markdown: A **pixel** is one tiny square of colour in a digital picture.
blocks.say: A digital picture is a grid of tiny coloured squares. Each square is called a pixel.

scenes.caption: Zoom.
scenes.say: Zara zooms in on the blue sky. She sees a few big squares.

scenes.caption: Many squares.
scenes.say: Each pixel has just one colour. Together, thousands of pixels make a smooth picture.

scenes.caption: Detail.
scenes.say: A photo with more pixels can show finer detail. A photo with few pixels looks blocky.

question.prompt: Zara zooms right in on a photo until she sees single coloured squares. What are they?
question.hint: A picture is built from them.
question.explanation: A digital picture is a grid of pixels.

blocks.markdown: To **crop** is to cut away the edges of a picture.
blocks.say: Zara wants only the mountains. She can cut away the sky and the road. That is cropping.

blocks.markdown: To **resize** is to make a picture bigger or smaller.
blocks.say: She can also make the whole picture bigger or smaller. That is called resizing it.

scenes.caption: Crop.
scenes.say: Zara drags a frame around the mountains. Everything outside the frame is cut away.

scenes.caption: Smaller.
scenes.say: Now she makes the cropped picture smaller. It fits on a postcard.

scenes.caption: Too big.
scenes.say: If she stretches a small picture very big, the pixels get blocky and blurry.

question.prompt: Cropping a photo adds new parts around its edges.
question.hint: Which way does a crop go?
question.explanation: A crop cuts parts away. It does not add anything.

blocks.title: Zara edits a Hunza photo
blocks.transcript: Zara has a photo from her family trip to Hunza. The sky looks grey. She zooms in. The picture is made of tiny coloured squares called pixels. She crops away the grey road. Now the mountains fill the picture. She makes the colours warmer. The sky turns a pale blue. She saves her edit as a new file. The original photo stays safe. A friend says, add a rainbow! But no rainbow was there that day. Zara says no. She writes, lightly edited by Zara, on her poster. She credits the photographer for a second photo. The poster is honest and fair.
blocks.caption: Zara edits a family photo from Hunza and learns to say what she changed.

points: A digital picture is a grid of pixels
Resize changes the size, and a big stretch can look blurry
blocks.say: Let us remember. Pictures are made of pixels. We can crop and resize them.

blocks.alt: A pink camellia flower with water droplets surrounded by dark green leaves and a wire fence
blocks.caption: A pink flower with raindrops. Editing can make the colours warmer, cooler or brighter.
blocks.credit: Photo by Laura Gilbert on Unsplash
blocks.say: Zara's pink flower photo looks cool and blue-green. She can recolour it so it looks warmer.

blocks.markdown: To **recolour** is to change colours. A **filter** changes the whole look in one go.
blocks.say: To recolour is to change the colours in a picture. A filter changes many colours at once.

scenes.caption: Dull.
scenes.say: Zara sees that the flower looks a little dull and cold.

scenes.caption: Warmer.
scenes.say: She makes the colours warmer. The pink glows and the leaves look golden.

scenes.caption: Same flower.
scenes.say: The flower is the same. Only the colours changed. A filter can do this in one click.

question.prompt: Zara paints the grey sky in her photo bright orange. What is this?

blocks.text: Stop 2: Clone and save a copy

blocks.markdown: The **clone** tool copies one part of a picture and pastes it somewhere else.
blocks.say: The clone tool copies one part of a picture onto another place. Zara uses it to hide a bin.

blocks.markdown: Keep the **original** safe. Edit a copy.
blocks.say: She always saves a copy first. The **original** stays safe, so she can start again.

scenes.caption: Copy.
scenes.say: Zara's photo has a bin on the grass. She copies a patch of clean grass.

scenes.caption: Paste.
scenes.say: She pastes the grass over the bin. The bin seems to vanish.

scenes.caption: Two files.
scenes.say: Her edit is saved as a new file. The original photo is untouched.

blocks.title: Sort the edits
blocks.goal: Move the 6 edits into Only improves the look or Changes the story.

blocks.title: Edit a copy
materials: A photo editing app or website, with a grown-up
instructions: Save a copy of your photo first.
Crop it, then try one recolour or filter.
Compare it with the original. Did the edit help or change the story?
blocks.say: Now you try. Ask a grown-up to help you edit one of your own photos.

question.prompt: The clone tool copies part of a picture to another place.
question.explanation: Cloning copies one part and pastes it elsewhere.

points: Recolour and filters change how colours look
Clone copies one part to another place
Edit a copy and keep the original
blocks.say: Let us remember. We can recolour, filter and clone. We always edit a copy.

terms.meaning: To change the colours in a picture.
A ready-made edit that changes the whole look of a picture.
To copy part of a picture and paste it somewhere else.
The first, unchanged version of a picture.
To change something.
Having more yellow and orange.

mini_quiz.explanation: A copy lets her start again and compare.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which tool can hide a bin by copying clean grass over it?
mini_quiz.explanation: The clone tool copies one part to another place.

blocks.markdown: A picture can be **edited** and still look real.
blocks.say: Many pictures online have been edited. Some edits are small. Some change what really happened.

scenes.caption: Shadows.
scenes.say: A photo shows a boy with a shadow pointing left. The tree shadow points right.

scenes.caption: Fuzzy edge.
scenes.say: Zara sees a fuzzy glowing line around one person. Something was pasted in.

scenes.caption: Twin clouds.
scenes.say: Two clouds look exactly the same, side by side. That may be cloning.

question.prompt: Zara sees one person with a fuzzy glowing outline in a photo. What might that mean?
question.explanation: A rough, glowing outline can show a pasted-in object.

options.text: That person may have been pasted in

blocks.markdown: A photo is only good **evidence** if we trust where it came from.
blocks.say: A photo can be used as evidence, but only if we know where it came from. Ask who took it.

blocks.markdown: Play the memory game. Then find the edited detail.
blocks.say: First a memory game. Then tap the detail that looks edited.

question.prompt: Tap the detail in this photo that looks edited.
question.hint: Look for a sharp, glowing outline.
question.explanation: A hard glowing edge suggests something was pasted in.

items.label: Balloon with a hard glowing edge
A tree with a soft shadow

points: Clues: odd shadows, glowing edges, copied parts
Ask who made the picture and where it came from
blocks.say: Let us remember. Edited pictures can look real. Check clues and ask where a picture came from.

terms.meaning: Changed using a program after it was taken.
Something that helps show what is true.
A small detail that helps you work something out.
A dark shape made when light is blocked.
Copied from one place and put in another.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which is a clue that a photo might be edited?
mini_quiz.explanation: Shadows from one sun should point the same way.

options.text: Two shadows that point different ways

mini_quiz.prompt: A photo that looks real cannot be edited.
mini_quiz.hint: Good edits are hard to see.
mini_quiz.explanation: Edited pictures can look completely real.

mini_quiz.prompt: What should you ask about a photo used as evidence?
mini_quiz.explanation: We trust a photo more if we know its source.

blocks.markdown: An honest poster tells the truth about its pictures.
blocks.say: Zara makes a poster about her Hunza trip. She picks a photo and thinks about the rules.

blocks.markdown: Use your own photos or ask **permission** first.
blocks.say: She only uses photos she has permission to use. Her own photos are the easiest choice.

blocks.markdown: Small fixes are fine. Do not mislead.
blocks.say: She crops and brightens her photo lightly. Small fixes do not change the story.

scenes.caption: Her photo.
scenes.say: Zara picks a photo she took herself in Hunza. She has full permission.

scenes.caption: Light edits.
scenes.say: She crops to the valley and makes it a little brighter. The scene is still true.

scenes.caption: No fake rainbow.
scenes.say: She does not add a rainbow that was never there. That would mislead people.

blocks.title: Plan an honest poster
materials: Two or three photos you may use
instructions: Choose photos you took or have permission to use.
Write a caption that says what each picture shows.
Note any edits, such as cropped or brightened.
blocks.say: Now you try. Plan a poster with a grown-up and check each picture.

question.prompt: Put the steps of making an honest poster in order.
question.explanation: Choose legally, edit lightly, say what changed, then credit.

items.text: Add a caption saying what you changed
Pick a photo you have permission to use

blocks.markdown: **Copyright** means the maker owns the picture. Give **credit** when you use it.
blocks.say: Every picture has a maker who owns it. That ownership is called copyright. We credit the maker.

scenes.caption: Owned.
scenes.say: Zara finds a lovely photo online. The photographer owns it.

scenes.caption: Check.
scenes.say: She checks if she is allowed to use it. She asks for permission when needed.

scenes.caption: Credit.
scenes.say: On her poster she writes the maker's name and where the photo came from.

question.prompt: An honest poster says when a picture has been edited.
question.explanation: Saying what you changed keeps a poster honest.

points: Use your own photos or ask permission
Light edits are fine, misleading edits are not
Credit the maker and say when you edited
blocks.say: Let us remember. Use pictures fairly, edit lightly and say what you changed.

terms.meaning: Being allowed to do something.
The rule that says the maker owns their work.
A note saying who made something.
Telling the truth.
To make someone believe something that is not true.
A large printed page with pictures and words.
